To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BAC vectors containing the entire CFTR gene with regulatory regions, derived from a single fragment and with a detailed map of the inserts, are suitable tools to study CFTR function and its role as a receptor for bacteria.

we have assembled two Bacterial Artificial Chromosomes (BACs) vectors containing a single CFTR genomic fragment with the regulatory regions, isolated in a single-step procedure and recovered in E. coli, and that these BACs contain a functional CF TR fragment, as shown by expression and functional analyses.
we have developed a novel approach for isolating BAC clones containing the CFTR locus with intact regulatory regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of BAC vectors for the CFTR gene and the expression of CFTR in model cells.
the development of a novel approach to the study of CFTR expression and function in human cells.
CFTR gene expression, activity and its interaction with P. aeruginosa in cells that have a functional CFTR channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these BAC vectors can be considered as the most suitable vectors for CFTR gene expression and activity studies, and can be used for gene transfer experiments.
the two BAC vectors contain the entire CFTR gene and are useful tools for functional studies of CFTR.
the BAC vector described in this study is a valuable tool for studying CFTR expression and CFTR function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BAC vector system is an efficient and reliable tool for the expression and functional analysis of the entire CFTR gene and its regulatory regions, and may be useful for other genes.

we have established a new BAC system to express CFTR from the human genomic locus, with intact BAc DNAs prepared for functional analyses, which will be useful for studies of CFTR expression and function in model cells, and in the development of CFTR-based therapies.
we have established a new model system that will be useful for studies of CFTR expression and function, and for studies of the CFTR-Pseudomonas aerugenosa interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BAC vectors are useful tools to study CFTR expression and function.
these BAC vectors can be used as a model for CFTR expression and function, and can serve as a tool for further functional analysis of the CFTR gene and for gene therapy.
the BAC vector is a useful and versatile system for studying CFTR expression and function.
